title: FASTER — Derived System Card (code-to-spec)
source: microsoft/FASTER @ 7f71289 (C++ in cc/src). Concurrent latch-free KV store, SIGMOD'18.
purpose: A concurrent, multi-core key-value store for point operations (Read/Upsert/RMW/Delete) over data that may exceed memory. Embedded C++ library; threads operate via pinned sessions on a latch-free hash index + an epoch-protected HybridLog.

operations: CompletePending (drive async I/O on a disk miss)
interface.semantics: Keys and values are USER-DEFINED templated types (FasterKv<Key,Value,Disk>); the user supplies GetHash, size, comparison, and atomic-put methods. Point operations only — no range scans.
interface.session_model: Each thread StartSession → operates → CompletePending → StopSession; operations may return Pending and complete via callback (async on SSD miss).

data_model.property: Compact 8-byte index entries; records live in the log
data_model.guarantee: Hash bucket = 64 bytes (7 entries + overflow ptr), each entry 8 bytes (48-bit address + 14-bit tag). Keys/values are NOT in the index — the entry points to a record in the HybridLog; records chain by a 48-bit previous-address pointer (collision list). Index stays small enough to be fully in RAM.
data_model.evidence: cc/src/index/hash_bucket.h:26 HashBucketEntry, :319 HotLogIndexHashBucket (64B); cc/src/core/record.h:15 RecordInfo (8B header); cc/src/core/address.h:20 Address (48-bit)

durability.guarantee: No per-write log. Periodic Checkpoint() captures the index + a HybridLog checkpoint without stopping the world (CPR: phases REST→PREPARE→IN_PROGRESS→WAIT_FLUSH→PERSISTENCE_CALLBACK), using a 13-bit per-record version to separate pre/post-checkpoint writes. Loss window = everything since the last completed checkpoint. Two HybridLog strategies: fold-over (in-place, faster recovery) vs snapshot file.
durability.evidence: cc/src/core/faster.h:3307 Checkpoint, :3436 Recover; cc/src/core/checkpoint_state.h; cc/src/core/state_transitions.h + phase.h; cc/src/core/record.h (checkpoint_version)

consistency.guarantee: After recovery, for any thread, if operation N is present then all that thread's prior operations are too — recovery keeps records with version ≤ checkpoint version and discards later ones. This is exactly the spec's monotonicity property; cross-thread ordering is NOT guaranteed.

memory_reclamation.property: HybridLog tiering + epoch-based page reclamation; natural caching
memory_reclamation.guarantee: The log's logical address space has three regions: mutable tail (in-place updates), read-only (read-copy-update), and on-disk (async I/O). Hot records stay hot by being copied to the tail; cold ones age out — a second-chance caching with NO per-record LRU stats. Pages are freed only via epoch trigger actions once all threads have passed the epoch (safe reclamation, not refcounting/hazard pointers).

concurrency.property: Latch-free CAS index + epoch synchronization + in-place updates
concurrency.guarantee: All index operations are 64-bit atomic CAS on hash entries — no latches; a tentative-bit two-phase insert prevents duplicates without locking. Hot-record updates happen in place (RMW can be a single atomic op) with no allocation or index change. The epoch framework (a shared monotonic counter + per-thread epochs + trigger actions) replaces locks for global state changes. Scales near-linearly across cores — the hot path has zero coordination.
concurrency.evidence: cc/src/index/hash_bucket.h:86 AtomicHashBucketEntry::compare_exchange_strong; cc/src/core/light_epoch.h Protect/Unprotect/BumpCurrentEpoch; cc/src/core/faster.h:285 InternalUpsert (in-place), :288 InternalRmw

partitioning.property: Single-node multi-threaded; F2 adds hot/cold tiering (not sharding)
partitioning.guarantee: One FasterKv instance shared by all threads; no network layer, no cross-machine sharding. The F2 variant (F2Kv) splits a hot in-memory store and a cold on-disk store with background compaction between them — a vertical tier, not a horizontal shard.

transactions.guarantee: Each Read/Upsert/RMW/Delete is individually atomic (RMW on a hot record = a single atomic instruction). There is no MULTI/transaction API and no cross-key atomicity — the contract is exactly the per-operation thread-safety a benchmark needs.

design_space_notes: FASTER's defining choices vs a from-scratch builder: latch-free multi-core index (max throughput) vs single-thread simplicity; HybridLog hot/cold tier (larger-than-memory at near-memory speed) vs evict-or-LSM; epoch reclamation vs locks/hazard pointers; checkpoint recovery (per-thread prefix) vs WAL; in-place updates (RMW = atomic op) vs copy-on-write.
